log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Connect each incident and its trace identifier to its severity and explanatory summary.","tasks":["Find an incident by its identifier.","Read or copy its trace ID.","Compare severity and scan summaries across incidents."],"relations":["Each row describes one incident; its trace ID, severity and summary belong together.","The incident and trace IDs support precise lookup, while severity and summary convey meaning."],"roles":["Column headers identify four distinct fields.","Each body row is one incident record; the incident ID is its practical anchor even though no row header is declared.","Severity is a short categorical field; summary is prose."],"keep_whole":["Incident IDs and trace IDs should remain intact for reliable lookup and copying when space permits.","Severity labels and individual prose words should remain whole."],"may_wrap":["Summary prose may wrap naturally between words.","The Incident header and other short headers should remain on one line where possible."],"same_scale":["All incident IDs share one column width, as do all trace IDs, severity labels and summaries.","Severity needs a compact width; summary needs more flexible space for prose."],"h_vs_v":"A viewport-fitting table avoids horizontal scrolling but must split long identifiers and produce tall, fragmented rows. Scrolling can preserve identifiers and severity labels, with additional width reducing prose wrapping at the cost of more horizontal travel."},"designs":[{"widths":[98,100,80,81],"strategy":"Fit the 359px viewport, reserving enough space for severity while accepting broken identifiers and heavily wrapped summaries."},{"widths":[165,299,80,150],"strategy":"Use a compact scrolling table that keeps identifiers and severity whole while wrapping summaries into a narrow prose column."},{"widths":[165,299,80,360],"strategy":"Use a spacious scrolling table that preserves identifiers and gives summaries room for more natural reading and shorter rows."}]}
